Marcus / Team,

I reviewed Acme's redlines. Below are our recommended positions and suggested counter-language. I kept the wording concise so it can be copy/pasted into the PDF redline: 

1) Availability target
- Acme asks for 99.9%. Proposed compromise: 99.9% for the first 6 months following go-live (to cover initial traffic patterns), then 99.95% thereafter. Suggested clause: "During the first 6 months after service activation, Redwood warrants 99.9% Monthly Uptime. Thereafter, Redwood warrants 99.95% Monthly Uptime."

2) Service credits
- Acme's scaling formula (25% for >=8 hours) is more aggressive than our standard. Proposed compromise: tiered credit with reasonable caps: 10% credit for monthly downtime >= 1 hour, 25% credit for >= 8 hours, with a 30% monthly cap and a 50% cumulative cap in any rolling 12-month period. Suggested clause: "Service Credits shall be calculated per Monthly Uptime period as follows: (i) Downtime >= 1 hour and < 8 hours: 10% of Monthly Fees; (ii) Downtime >= 8 hours: 25% of Monthly Fees. Monthly cap: 30%. Cumulative 12-month cap: 50%. Credits are Redwood's sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures."

3) P1 response times
- 15-minute initial response is operationally risky for distributed support. Proposal: accept 15-minute acknowledgment for our Premium support add-on only. For standard support included in the order form: 1-hour initial acknowledgement and 4-hour mitigation plan. Suggested clause: "For Customers on the Premium Support plan, Redwood will acknowledge P1 incidents within 15 minutes. For standard support, acknowledgements will be within 1 hour with a documented mitigation plan initiated within 4 hours."

4) Maintenance notifications
- 7 days notice is reasonable for scheduled production-impacting maintenance. We can accept 7 days for maintenance that changes API behavior or may cause downtime, but retain 48h for routine infra patches that do not change API semantics. Suggested clause: "Redwood will provide at least seven (7) days’ advance notice for planned maintenance likely to impact Production API behavior or availability; routine maintenance that does not alter API behavior will be communicated at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance."

Next steps: if Acme accepts the compromise language above, we can generate a counter-redline and route to our legal for sign-off. If any of these are deal-blockers for Acme, flag them and Marcus will scope an exec touchpoint.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Sr. Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
